::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** June 17th. [1891][^2]  
**From:** 11 Bexley Terrace Torquay  
**Manuscript:** MS UCLA collection 100 box 119/1[^1]
:::

My dear Miss Yonge,
I have ventured to send you a [story](other_books/otherbook_644.qmd) for the Christmas number of the M.P. on the ‘rolling stone.’ I hope it is not too long—as far as I could reckon, it is shorter than one of those in a former number. You must forgive my infringing the editorial rules, and not letting the MS. pass through the publishers [sic] hands first.

Yours very sincerely
[Anna H. Drury](people/person_445.qmd)

---

[^1]: Black-edged paper.
[^2]: ‘The China Cupboard’ *MP* (1 January 1891) 108,  announced a competition for prize stories to be published in the extra Christmas number, on the subject of ‘A rolling stone gathers no moss’, the deadline for entries being 31 July 1891.
